slides.texte_overlay:
How to stay close to old friends
when life gets busy
Put a recurring date in the calendar. The first Friday of every month, a yearly weekend away. Friendships survive on plans that repeat.
Send small messages often. A photo that reminds you of them, a quick "how's the new job?" Little contact keeps you close between meetings.
Call instead of texting sometimes. Hearing someone's voice brings you back together much faster than a hundred messages.
Show up for the big moments. Weddings, births, funerals, hospital visits. Missing those is what really makes friends drift apart.
Before: I had nothing new to tell old friends. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and our calls are full of stories again.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I had nothing new to tell old friends. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Our calls are full of stories again.

slides.texte_overlay: Accept that friendships change. You won't see each other every week anymore. A good friendship can survive long gaps.
Be the one who organises. Someone has to book the table. Being that person is how you keep your best friends for life.
